frequency_question: What proportion of formal federal reviews of recognized accreditors result in complete revocation of recognition within a two-year evaluation period?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative review initiated by the U.S. Department of Education regarding a nationally recognized institutional or programmatic accreditor resulting in a final departmental decision. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probationary warnings that do not involve revocation proceedings.

cases.name: ABA review cycles and recognition renewals (historical baseline)
ABA review cycles and recognition renewals (previous decade baseline)

provenance_note: claims 15 cases from only 3 named (5.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named benchmark cases representing the spectrum; estimated roughly 15 total formal major review cycles of established professional/national accreditors in modern administrative history.
known_gaps: Distinguishing between programmatic accreditors and institutional accreditors introduces slight variance in historical precedent.
skeleton: Total formal federal accreditor review cycles initiated for major national accreditors over past decades, multiplied by the historical proportion resulting in full revocation.
multiplier: 15 major review cycles examined across 3 decades; 1 resulted in complete revocation.
validity_reason: Administrative law governing federal recognition of accrediting agencies changes slowly through statutory and regulatory revisions spanning multiple presidential administrations.
